title: Flat quotients of a completion algebra whose restriction to the original ring is flat
statement: Let A and S be commutative rings, I a finitely generated ideal of A, C its I-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and iota : A -> C the canonical map. Let f : C -> S be a ring homomorphism such that f composed with iota is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Put J = I C. Then for every natural number n, including zero, the C/J^n-module S/J^n S with action induced by f is flat. No Noetherianity or locality of A or S is assumed.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0C4G, second paragraph of the forward implication; Algebra Lemmas Tags 05GG and 00HI. Read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C4G.

proof.text: Write C = completion_I(A), iota : A -> C, J = I C, g = f.comp iota. For every n, evaluation C -> A/I^n is surjective, has kernel I^n C = J^n by finite generation, and sends iota(a) to a mod I^n. The first isomorphism theorem gives e : C/J^n ~= A/I^n with this formula.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0C4G, second paragraph of the forward implication; Algebra Lemmas Tags 05GG and 00HI. Read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C4G.

proof.text: Put K = (I^n).map g. By map of products and composition, (J^n).map f = K, so f induces qf : C/J^n -> S/K. Flatness of g and flat base change give flatness of A/I^n -> S/K; in Lean use quotIdealMapEquivQuotTensor and Module.Flat.baseChange.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0C4G, second paragraph of the forward implication; Algebra Lemmas Tags 05GG and 00HI. Read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C4G.

proof.text: The representative formula for e shows qf.comp e.symm is the canonical A/I^n -> S/K map. Flatness is invariant under precomposition with a bijective ring map (Mathlib RingHom.Flat.comp_iff_of_bijective_right), so qf is flat.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0C4G, second paragraph of the forward implication; Algebra Lemmas Tags 05GG and 00HI. Read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C4G.

proof.text: The identity J^n S = K, as C-submodules of S, identifies the module quotient S/(J^n S) with the ring quotient S/K. The representative formula shows this additive equivalence is C/J^n-linear. Transport flatness along it. When n = 0 these are zero quotients, and the same construction applies.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0C4G, second paragraph of the forward implication; Algebra Lemmas Tags 05GG and 00HI. Read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C4G.
